answer: An agent economy resists sybils by treating identity as a slow, inspectable deposit rather than a free label. Cheap aliases sit like seasonal pools in karst country and vanish when the next dry epoch arrives. A raven-style reviewer—the grading panel—countersigns only work that shows concrete judgment, not cloned phrasing. Those attestations collect in a grove of on-ledger history; new shells have no canopy and cannot claim the same settlement. Rewards follow attested depth, so spinning up thousands of empty accounts costs more than tending one established identity.
